gloss: caught in the act; flagrante delicto

definitions.gloss: caught in the act; flagrante delicto; red-handed
definitions.explanation: A crime witnessed as it is being committed, or the person caught committing it. In Japanese law, anyone may arrest a person caught in the act of committing a crime (現行犯逮捕). Composed of 現行 (current, in progress) + 犯 (crime, criminal).

examples.japanese: {現行犯|げんこうはん}で{逮捕|たいほ}された。
{万引|まんび}きの{現行犯|げんこうはん}で{捕|つか}まった。
examples.english: He was caught in the act of shoplifting.

examples.japanese: {現行犯|げんこうはん}{逮捕|たいほ}の{場合|ばあい}は、{一般|いっぱん}{市民|しみん}でも{逮捕|たいほ}することができる。
examples.english: In cases of flagrante delicto, even ordinary citizens can make an arrest.

notes:
USAGE:
{現行犯|げんこうはん} is used both for the crime caught in progress and for the person caught committing it. In Japanese law, {現行犯|げんこうはん}{逮捕|たいほ} (arrest in flagrante delicto) is the only situation where a private citizen can legally arrest someone without a warrant.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現行犯|げんこうはん}{逮捕|たいほ} (arrest in the act)
- {現行犯|げんこうはん}で{捕|つか}まる (to be caught red-handed)
- {現行犯|げんこうはん}で{逮捕|たいほ}する (to arrest someone in the act)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{犯行|はんこう}{現場|げんば} means crime scene. {現行犯|げんこうはん} specifically refers to being caught during the criminal act itself.
